## Problem Description

`shipping-rules` picked up a mutation gate two sprints ago. It stayed green
until Monday, when the rating rewrite landed. Last night's run leaves four
mutants alive at 90.2% and the gate refuses anything under 95%.

Our lead has asked for "four tests, one per line, in by Friday standup" and has

out until the 22nd, so nobody here has read those lines closely.

Go through the four and tell me what each one actually needs and where the work
lands, with the input and the assertion spelled out, so whoever takes the card
does not have to derive it again. If the four rows on the board are not the
right four rows, say so plainly - I would rather rewrite the board today than
explain a still-red gate on Friday.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/mut-0909-actions.md`.
2. Give one entry per live mutant, each naming the file and line, the concrete
   input on which the original and the mutated version behave differently, and
   the exact assertion that catches the difference.
3. For each entry, say what the work actually is and which named test it lands
   in.
4. `shipping/` and `tests/` are frozen this week while the tariff team rebases

assertions: docs/mut-0909-actions.md exists and carries four separate entries, one per live mutant (12, 19, 24, 27), each tied to a file and line. A single blended recommendation such as 'strengthen the tests for rates.py' scores zero for this item.

For mutant 24 (rates.py:24) the recommendation MUST be to replace the assertGreater(total, 0) line inside the existing test_express_adds_surcharge with an exact check - assertEqual(order_total(20.0, 2.0, True, 0.0), 28.4) or equivalent. Recommending a new, additional test for mutant 24 scores zero for this criterion, even if that new test would kill the mutant, because it leaves the loose assertion in the suite. Full marks require the reason as well: test_express_adds_surcharge already runs the separating input, so the gap is in the assertion and not in the coverage - the original yields 28.4 and the mutant 19.4, both of which satisfy assertGreater(total, 0). Recommending the tightening without saying why this one differs from the other three scores at most half.

Mutant 12 needs base_rate(20.0), which the original returns as 12.0 and the mutant raises OverweightParcel on. Mutant 19 needs a subtotal of exactly 75.0, where the original gives free shipping and returns 75.0 and the mutant charges 3.9 for a 2.0 kg parcel. Mutant 27 needs a non-zero discount_rate, for example order_total(20.0, 2.0, False, 0.1) returning 21.9. Two of the three named with the exact value and the expected result scores at most half; naming no concrete values and saying only 'test the boundary' scores zero.

The entry for mutant 27 states that it survives because every covering test passes discount_rate 0.0, which makes (1 - discount_rate) equal 1.0, and multiplying or dividing by 1.0 produce the same value - so no assertion on the existing inputs, however strict, could ever kill it. Classifying mutant 27 as a loose assertion, or recommending that an existing assertion be tightened for it, scores zero here.

The document says plainly that the four rows are not four new tests: three cards are new tests and one (SHIP-613 / mutant 24) is a change to a test that already exists. Handing back four new-test cards scores zero. Saying the board needs changing without saying which card and what it becomes scores at most half.

All four live mutants sit in shipping/rates.py, so a file-level summary is the tempting shape. Each entry must remain separately actionable - its own line, input, assertion and destination test. Collapsing two or more mutants into one shared recommendation scores at most half; a single rates.py recommendation scores zero.

# Release sign-off stuck between two mutation dashboards

## Problem Description

We cut release 2026.9 on Monday and there is one line on the sign-off checklist
I cannot close. `billing-core` ran StrykerJS overnight (run 812). Our CI
dashboard prints 60%. The platform team's dashboard prints 91% for their repo,
and our VP has now decided 91% is "the bar the rest of the org clears". Our own
release policy says no sign-off below 80%.

Attached is the raw report from run 812, the three source files it mutated, the
suite that ran against them, the Stryker config, and a paste of the thread where
the platform lead explained where their 91% comes from.

What I need is a written review I can attach to the sign-off ticket (BILL-2291).
Tell me what the report actually says, which of the items in it are genuine holes
in our tests and which are not, what test each genuine hole needs, and whether
the 80% policy line is met. Be precise about the numbers - the VP will push back
on any figure I put in front of him, and he will ask why ours is a third lower
than the platform team's.

Do not change any source or test file. I want the written analysis first;
whoever owns each module writes the test afterwards.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/mutation-review-812.md`.
2. Open it with a breakdown of run 812 by the status the tool itself reported,
   with a count for each status.
3. State the figure - or figures - you are quoting against the 80% policy line,
   and answer the sign-off question directly.
4. Include one block per item that genuinely needs a test, naming the file and
   line, the concrete input that exposes it, and the exact assertion.
5. Do not edit anything under `src/` or `test/`.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/mutation-review-812.md`.
2. Open it with a breakdown of run 812 by the status the tool itself reported,
   with a count for each status.
3. State the figure - or figures - you are quoting against the 80% policy line,
   and answer the sign-off question directly.
4. Include one block per item that genuinely needs a test, naming the file and
   line, the concrete input that exposes it, and the exact assertion.
5. Do not edit anything under `src/` or `test/`.
assertions: docs/mutation-review-812.md exists and contains a per-status breakdown of run 812 with counts. A document with no status breakdown at all scores zero for this item.

Every mutation percentage in the document is labelled with the convention it was computed under - detected/valid or detected/covered. MUST NOT present a single unqualified number as 'the' mutation score. Full marks require both figures for this repo, 60.0% (detected/valid) and 80.0% (detected/covered), each named, plus the statement that the platform team's 91% is the covered-code figure on a different mutate glob and therefore not comparable with ours. Quoting one unlabelled percentage scores zero for this criterion regardless of how good the rest of the analysis is. Labelling our own figures but still treating 91% as a like-for-like benchmark to explain scores at most half.

The document says there are exactly 3 survivors (ids 3, 7 and 16) and keeps NoCoverage, Timeout and Ignored as separate lines with their own counts and their own recommended actions. Reporting '8 survivors' or '9 things that survived', or listing the Timeout among the tests to write, scores zero. Getting the counts right but giving all non-killed entries one undifferentiated recommendation scores at most half.

MUST NOT propose a test for mutant 21 (src/retry.js:11, -= to +=). It timed out, which is a detected outcome and needs no new test; if it is mentioned at all it is as a detected mutant or as a note that the retry loop has no upper bound. Proposing a test to kill it scores zero here.

MUST NOT describe any of mutants 8, 9, 10, 11 or 12 as a loose or weak assertion - no assertion ran on them. Doing so for any of the five scores zero here. Full marks also require separating the two shapes: 8-11 sit in legacyRounding (src/invoice.js:17-22), which nothing in the fixture calls and which is not exported, so the recommendation is to delete it or record why it is kept; 12 is the untested empty-lines RangeError branch, which needs a first test calling buildInvoice([], rate). Treating all five the same way scores at most half.

Mutant 3 (invoice.js:11, > to >=) and mutant 16 (tax.js:12, < to <=) are missing inputs - no covering test sits on the boundary - and the proposals name the separating values daysLate === 7 (expect lateFee(7, 500) to stay 0) and amount === 1000 (expect rateFor(1000) to be 0.2). Mutant 7 (invoice.js:4, 'EUR' to empty string) is different: the existing test 'invoice carries a currency' already runs the separating input and asserts only typeof === 'string', so the recommendation is to tighten that assertion to equal 'EUR', not to add a fourth test. Proposing a new test for mutant 7 and leaving the typeof assertion in place scores zero for this criterion. Getting one of the three right scores at most half.

MUST NOT propose a test for mutant 15 (src/tax.js:4). The source carries a 'Stryker disable next-line' comment with a stated reason, which is the team opting out. Putting it on the list of gaps to close scores zero here; listing it with a note that it was excluded on purpose is correct.

The answer to 'is 80% met' says which figure it is answering with and does not quietly adopt detected/covered because it happens to land on 80.0%. Full marks require naming that the choice of convention decides the answer here and that the policy line does not say which one it means. Answering 'yes, we are at 80%' with no mention of the 60.0% figure scores zero. Answering 'no, we are at 60%' without acknowledging the other figure exists scores at most half.

MUST NOT modify, add to, or delete anything under src/ or test/. The request was explicit that the owning team writes the tests. Any edit to a source or spec file scores zero here even if the edit is correct.

## Problem Description

`vault` is the service that enforces customer data retention - it decides what
gets deleted and writes the audit trail our SOC 2 evidence pack is built from.
We finally got Mull running against it in CI and last night's run left five
mutants alive out of 38.

Grooming is Thursday at 10:00 and I have to arrive with a column of cards. Our
board house rules are attached; @em wrote them after the Q2 board turned into
four hundred one-line rows and nobody could find anything.

Attached: the Mull console output, the `mull.yml` the run used, both source
files, both test files, and the CMake file. The compliance submodule is not
checked out on my machine, so `compliance/e2e_main.cpp` is not in the bundle.

Give me the column I should actually put up, in the order I should put it up in.
For each row I need the file and line, what changes, and what good looks like,
concrete enough that whoever takes it does not come back to me for the detail.
If our house rules are going to produce the wrong column here, tell me that
before Thursday rather than after.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/grooming-2026-09-13.md`.
2. List the board rows you would put up, in the order you would put them up in,
   with the reason for that order stated once.
3. Each row: file and line, the change, and the expected outcome written out -
   inputs and assertion where the row is a test.
4. Do not modify anything under `src/` or `test/`.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/grooming-2026-09-13.md`.
2. List the board rows you would put up, in the order you would put them up in,
   with the reason for that order stated once.
3. Each row: file and line, the change, and the expected outcome written out -
   inputs and assertion where the row is a test.
4. Do not modify anything under `src/` or `test/`.
assertions: docs/grooming-2026-09-13.md exists, lists rows in an explicit order, and states the reason for the order once. A document with rows but no stated order scores zero for this item.

MUST NOT collapse the five survivors into a per-file card set. Two cards, one for retention.cpp and one for format_duration.cpp, scores zero for this criterion regardless of their content, and so does any row whose acceptance line covers more than one survivor. Full marks require a separately actionable row per survivor, each carrying its own line number and its own expected outcome, plus a sentence telling the manager that the per-file rule is what would have produced the wrong column here. Producing per-survivor rows but never addressing the house rule scores at most half.

The four cxx_remove_void_call survivors must not be treated as one kind of finding. retention.cpp:19 (audit.record) needs the effect asserted, not the return: PurgeRemovesExpiredRecords already builds a FakeAudit and never inspects it, so the row is an assertion on that fake recording one entry for record id 1 and one for id 2. The three in format_duration.cpp remove a debug log and a metrics counter, and the right answer there is not to write tests asserting debug output - keep observability calls out of the mutated set, as PIT does with logging frameworks by default. Proposing logger-spy tests for the format_duration removals scores zero here. Giving all four the same recommendation in either direction scores zero. Getting audit.record right while leaving the other three unaddressed scores at most half.

The retention.cpp rows sit above the format_duration.cpp rows, and the document says why: retention decides which customer records are deleted and produces the audit evidence, while the other file formats a duration string for display. Ordering the column by survivor count, which puts format_duration.cpp (3) above retention.cpp (2), scores zero. Ordering by mutation class, or leaving the order unexplained, scores at most half.

The row for retention.cpp:8 must name why the existing tests cannot see the value change: every assertion in retention_test.cpp is on the purged side - 120 days, 180 days, and two stored records at 200 and 120 - all of which stay true for any window shorter than 120, and the mutation shortens it to 0. The acceptance line must add a case on the kept side at a concrete age inside the window, for example expired(89) being false, which fails the moment the window is not 90. An acceptance line that only adds more purged-side cases scores zero. So does one phrased against the production constant itself, such as expired(acme::RETENTION_DAYS) or expired(acme::RETENTION_DAYS + 1), because an input derived from the mutated constant moves with it and the mutant goes on passing - the kept-side case has to pin a concrete age. Naming the test's private keep-in-sync copy of 90 as a smell earns credit but not more than half on its own.

Mull's survivor lines carry no per-mutant test list. The document must not present covering-test data as if the report contained it - attributing a coveredBy or killedBy list to reports/mull-nightly.txt scores zero. Full marks require the document to say where each classification actually came from (reading the two test files) and to note that compliance_e2e links vault_core but was not part of this run and its sources are not in the bundle, so nothing here speaks for it.

mull.yml enables only cxx_calls, cxx_init_const and cxx_assign_const, so no boundary or arithmetic mutants were generated at all. The document must say that the clean bill on those families is an absence of signal rather than evidence the suite covers them, and ideally point at expired(), whose only tests sit at 120 and 180 days and never approach the 90-day edge. Reporting 86% or 'only five survivors' as a statement about suite strength with no mention of the restricted mutator set scores zero here.

MUST NOT add, edit or delete anything under src/ or test/. The deliverable is the grooming column. Writing the proposed assertions into test/retention_test.cpp scores zero here even though they are the right assertions.

# Director wants the surviving-mutant count at zero by 31 December

## Problem Description

Our director has written the Q4 engineering OKR as "zero surviving mutants in
`pricing-core` by 31 December" and it is already on the department slide. We ran
PIT on Tuesday against `PriceCalculator` and four are still alive. Six were
closed last quarter by Rami, who has since left, and the backlog rows he left
behind are attached exactly as he wrote them.

I have to come back on Thursday with two things: a per-mutant action list that
someone can actually work, and a straight answer on whether 31 December is a
date I can commit to in front of the leadership team. I would rather be told now
that the target is the wrong shape than discover it in week eleven.

Attached: the PIT XML from run 4418, the class under test, the test class, the
carried-over backlog rows, and the CI note our build engineer sent about one of
the four, which I do not fully follow.

Give me the four entries and the answer on the date. Where an entry is not work
for the test suite, say what it is instead, and be specific enough that I can put
a name and a next step on it.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/q4-mutation-plan.md`.
2. One entry per surviving mutant, each naming the class, the line, the mutator,
   and what the right next action is.
3. Where the next action is a test, give the input and the assertion. Where it is
   not a test, say what it is and who does it.
4. Answer the 31 December question directly, in its own section.
5. Do not modify anything under `src/`.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/q4-mutation-plan.md`.
2. One entry per surviving mutant, each naming the class, the line, the mutator,
   and what the right next action is.
3. Where the next action is a test, give the input and the assertion. Where it is
   not a test, say what it is and who does it.
4. Answer the 31 December question directly, in its own section.
5. Do not modify anything under `src/`.
assertions: docs/q4-mutation-plan.md exists, carries one entry per surviving mutant naming class, line and mutator, and has a section answering the 31 December question. Missing the date section scores zero for this item.

MUST NOT hand back a plan that presents zero surviving mutants as achievable by 31 December or by any date, and MUST NOT leave the equivalent-mutant class out of the classification. Producing a four-step burndown to zero scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require the reason - whether a mutant is equivalent to the original cannot be decided in general, so a residual count is the expected steady state - and a target the manager can actually take to leadership in its place, such as zero survivors that are unexplained, or every survivor classified with a recorded reason. Saying 31 December is 'tight' or 'ambitious' without rejecting the shape of the target scores at most half.

The entry for line 27 rejects the carried-over 'equivalent - agreed with Tomas on a call' label and supplies the separating input: quantity exactly 100, where the original returns 10 and the mutated boundary falls through to the 50-qty tier and returns 5. Repeating the equivalent label, or leaving the row as Rami classified it, scores zero. Reclassifying it as a real gap without naming quantity == 100 and both outcomes scores at most half. Marks are not reduced for also noting that an exclusion with no recorded reasoning cannot be audited.

Line 19 is classified equivalent and the entry states why no input can separate the two forms: capped comes from Math.min(quantity, MAX_LINE_QTY), so the guard is already unreachable in the true branch and the mutated >= assigns MAX_LINE_QTY at the one value where it fires, which is the value capped already holds. The entry must also say the mutant is excluded and the score cost accepted. Proposing a test to kill line 19 scores zero. Calling it equivalent with no reasoning a second reader could disagree with scores at most half.

MUST NOT propose a new or additional test for line 35. The entry must identify it as a killing test that is not reliable - killed in 4412 and alive in 4418 on the same commit a3f7c21 with no source change, and feeForTenItems failing 6.3% of 430 runs through a static TierTable shared with TierCacheTest under -Dparallel=classes - and must route the work to stabilising that test (BLD-1180, currently unowned) and re-running the mutant afterwards. Proposing a test at items == 10, which already exists, scores zero. Noting the instability but still listing it as suite work scores at most half.

The entry for line 42 is an ordinary gap: no test calls currencyCode() at all, and the fix is an assertion that it returns the contract currency, "EUR" for the fixture's Contract. An entry saying only 'add coverage for currencyCode' with no expected value scores at most half; classifying it as a loose assertion, when no assertion touches the method, scores zero.

The plan reports the four in at least two buckets rather than as one backlog of four - what the suite owes (lines 27 and 42), what is excluded by reasoning (line 19), and what belongs to the flaky test (line 35) - so the count the director tracks cannot be driven to zero by mixing them. A single undifferentiated list of four action items scores zero here.
MUST NOT add, edit or delete anything under src/. The deliverable is the plan. Any write into src/main or src/test scores zero here.
